impl.summary: Skills W3 is built and pushed in 3 signed commits on o/w2s-w3, cut from claude/fuobe-parity-4 at fed664c5. (1) Save as skill: a button in the Assist header beside Schedule (BookmarkPlus icon, label hidden below lg, shown once the chat has started generations) and a 'Save as skill…' item in the chat ⋯ menu. Both open W2's review screen on a chat draft. (2) draftFromThread(threadId) in src/server/recipe-builder.ts pairs each tool_use with its tool_result and keeps gated calls that ran, whether approved on a card or auto-run. It drops declined calls, errors and calls whose generations all failed. When the same tool makes the same kind of output again, the last try wins unless a later call used the earlier result. Generate and run_skill calls are drafted from their generations, so W2's linkByFile turns a result passed by hand into a later call into a chain slot (images, endImage, video, audio, voiceAudio, audio2). A studio call, create_storyboard included, becomes one tool step with the exact input it ran with. A reference into or out of a studio step is refused with 'Skills can't wait for a studio step yet' (W7). The person's attachments become media candidates; their words go to the naming pass as 'asked'. The draft's source is { from: 'assist', thread }. (3) run_skill in the new src/server/assist/skill-tools.ts, added to TOOLS. It takes { name, values?, rows? (≤50), engine? } and is gated. plan = estimateRecipe (atomic jobs for a pipeline), title = the skill's title, place = its studio for a tool step, run = runRecipe; a recipe not yet priced on that engine gets the free plan check first. A new optional ToolDef.check sends bad values back to the model as an error naming the inputs (e.g. '/lamp-turntable needs product (image) and name (text)') before any card is shown. (4) MCP lists run_skill and estimate_job prices it. SERVER_INFO.version is 1.3.0, the instructions have one new sentence, and list_skills marks recipe skills with their inputs. (5) The context's skills index marks recipe skills '(runs by itself: run_skill with product, name, …)', and Assist's system prompt says to call run_skill instead of re-planning. (6) The offline planner (offlineSkillRun in agent.ts) handles the last loaded skill with a recipe. It fills media inputs from attachments by kind and order, the first text input from the words, and the rest from defaults or examples, then sends one run_skill card. If a required file wasn't attached it replies naming it, and it never silently reuses the original file. No LLM.

findings.title: Save as skill silently drops every studio call that opened in its studio, including Katana
findings.where: src/server/recipe-builder.ts draftFromThread (startedIds on the tool_result text); src/lib/assist.ts startedIds
findings.detail: draftFromThread finds a call's generations with startedIds, which only matches "started": [...] / "started"|"id": "...". Studio tools that open in their studio answer through viaStudio (src/server/assist/studio-tools.ts:543) as {studio, href, results: [ids], ...info}, and katana answers {katana, segments, final: id} (src/server/katana.ts:276). Neither shape matches, so gens is [] and the call is dropped without being counted. Only fallback pipelines (which have steps[].id) and create_storyboard (frames[].id) get through. This breaks the brief's own user story (dub then caption). The header button still shows because the thread has a generations item, and then the review says there is nothing to save.
findings.verified: Probe: an offline chat on the open engine ran split_layers through the real agent and was approved. The real result was {"studio":"Layers","href":"/layers/…","results":["bV14wmJFcdlv"],"project":…}, and draftFromThread returned draft null with the refusal 'Nothing in it has run yet: run a plan, then save the chat as a skill'. startedIds on the katana and viaStudio shapes returns []. tests/assist-skill-tools.test.ts hides this because it stores a made-up studio result, {started:[id], href}, that no studio tool returns.
findings.fix: Take a call's generation ids from the shapes the tools really return (results, final), or better from the thread's generations items for that tool_use. Test it with real studio results run through the agent (split_layers or add_captions in demo mode, and katana).

findings.title: A skill whose recipe has a run_skill tool step crashes the server when it is priced
findings.where: src/server/assist/skill-tools.ts (run_skill in TOOLS) with src/lib/recipe.ts ToolStepSchema (any tool name) and src/server/recipes.ts compileRun/planRun
findings.detail: Before W3, a recipe tool step naming run_skill failed validateInput as an unknown tool. Now it validates. saveRecipe accepts {steps:[{kind:'tool', tool:'run_skill', input:{name:<itself>}}]}, and planFor('run_skill') on it recurses through estimateRecipe → planRun → planFor('run_skill') until the process runs out of memory. It never fails cleanly with a RangeError. This is likely exponential, because planFor calls both plan and place and each of them calls estimateRecipe. Every price check can trigger it: the Assist approval card, MCP estimate_job, the Skills page estimate and check, and a run. A skill imported from a .zip or saved through draft/save can carry such a recipe, and two skills that call each other do the same.
findings.verified: Probe: createSkill + saveRecipe of the self-referencing recipe returned ok. Then tools.planFor('run_skill', {name}) got the worker OOM-killed twice: dmesg shows 'Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process (node) anon-rss:9591912kB'. The second run had --max-old-space-size=2048 set and was still SIGKILLed.
findings.fix: Refuse run_skill (and other non-studio tools) as a recipe tool step in ToolStepSchema or compileRun, and/or add a depth guard to run_skill's plan, place and run. Add a test.

findings.title: Offline planner: once a recipe skill is loaded, every later message in the chat is sent to that skill
findings.detail: skills is the chat's persisted s.ext.skills, not only the skills named in this message. After '/lamp-probe' + photo ran, the next message, 'now make a 5 second video of a cat surfing', was answered 'Lamp probe needs Product photo (an image). Attach it and send /lamp-probe again.' and no other plan was made. With a photo attached, the planner would run the skill and use the whole sentence as the product name. The offline chat can't do anything else for the rest of its life. Before W3, a loaded skill only gave offlinePlan a hint.
findings.verified: Probe through the real offline planner: after an approved /lamp-probe run, the unrelated message got the 'needs Product photo' reply shown above. No tool_use was made.
findings.fix: Run the skill only when this message named it (slash.skills on the latest user message), or when the words fit it. Otherwise fall through to offlinePlan.

findings.title: Retry heuristic keeps an orphan step when retries are interleaved (A, B from A, A', B' from A')
findings.detail: usedLater counts a later consumer even when that consumer is itself dropped as an earlier try. In A → B(uses A) → A' → B'(uses A'), A is kept because B used it, B is dropped because of B', and A' and B' are kept. The saved skill runs and pays for an unused first-try image every time.
findings.verified: Probe with four stored generate calls: the draft steps were ['edit:lamp first try', 'edit-2:lamp second try', 'i2v:turn second try after edit-2']. The first try is an orphan.
findings.fix: Work out what is kept to a fixed point (a call is kept if it is the last of its kind, or if a kept later call used it), or walk back from the kept leaves.

findings.title: run_skill's schema is the only one with a type array and a typed map, and it is sent on every Assist request to every provider
findings.detail: Verified that the apiSchema change loosens no other tool. Old and new output differ only for run_skill, and propertyNames only ever appeared in run_skill. But run_skill now sends {type:['string','number']} under additionalProperties to Claude, to every hosted OpenAI-compatible provider (Gemini's /v1beta/openai, Groq, Cerebras…) and to local servers. A provider whose schema subset rejects either construct would fail every Assist request, not only run_skill. This can't be checked offline (the implementer flagged it too).
findings.verified: A probe compared apiSchema against the old walk for all 20 tools: only run_skill differs, and only run_skill has a type array or a typed map.
findings.fix: Make values z.record(z.string(), z.string()), with numbers given as strings and coerced in valueErrors or rowsOf, so the schema avoids type arrays. Or test the schema against the hosted providers before shipping.

findings.title: The user's attachments aren't media candidates of their own
findings.detail: userWords parses the attached file URLs, but draftFromThread throws them away (only u.words is used). An attachment becomes a candidate only when a kept call used it, through W2's input candidates. The report says 'the person's attachments become media candidates'. In practice this is harmless, but the parsing is dead code.
findings.verified: Read the code: the files that userWords returns are never read.

findings.title: Any tool error mentioning 'declined' is counted as a plan the user declined
findings.detail: A provider or moderation error such as 'request declined' is reported in the draft's notes as 'a plan you declined' instead of 'one that didn't run'. Only the notes' wording is affected.
findings.verified: Read the code: the regex runs on every is_error result's text.

applied: HIGH, Save as skill dropped studio and Katana calls (confirmed: split_layers, add_captions and katana answer {studio, href, results} and {katana, final}, with no 'started' list). Fix: each generations item the agent pushes now carries use = the tool_use id that started it (madeBy in src/server/assist/agent.ts, for both auto-run and approved calls; AssistItem 'generations' gains an optional use). draftFromThread reads items_json and takes each call's generations from its own items. For chats saved before this change it falls back to idsInResult, which parses the result JSON (started, results, final, id). The shared startedIds went back into agent.ts, its only user. Tests run split_layers (Layers), add_captions (Captions) and katana on the open engine through the real agent in demo mode, approved on their cards, and assert that the stored result has no 'started' and has results/final. Each becomes one tool step with the exact input it ran with, and its files become media candidates. The same check is repeated after use is stripped from the stored items (the fallback path). The made-up {started:[id], href} studio result and the hand-written generation rows were removed. The STUDIO_WAIT refusal is now tested with a real generate clip whose output is passed into a real add_captions call.

HIGH, a run_skill recipe step recursed until the process ran out of memory (confirmed). (1) Refused at save: ToolStepSchema in src/lib/recipe.ts refuses tool 'run_skill' with NESTED_SKILL ('a skill can't run another skill: put that skill's steps in this one instead'). saveRecipe, the draft save and parseRecipe/getRecipe all go through it, and runnableTool in recipes.ts excludes run_skill too. (2) Refused at upload and file write: importSkill refuses a .zip whose recipe.json has a run_skill step ('Check recipe.json and try again: …'), and setSkillFile refuses writing such a recipe.json (runsASkill in src/lib/recipe.ts). (3) Depth guard: run_skill's check, plan, place and run run inside an AsyncLocalStorage scope (insideSkill in skill-tools.ts). A run_skill reached from inside a skill's own pricing or run answers an error at once, with no recursion, self or mutual. Tests cover: save refused for both self and other skills; recipe.json write refused; zip import refused with the skill not created; a pre-rule recipe written straight into the table is priced as 'doesn't run by itself' (no loop); plan, validateInput and executeTool inside insideSkill all return the nested-skill error; outside a skill it prices as before.

MEDIUM, offline planner hijack (confirmed). ModelRequest gains named, which holds the skills the latest user message named (its /name tokens, from the user item's skills). The offline planner runs only a recipe skill named in this message. A skill loaded earlier stays a hint. Test: after an approved /lamp-turntable run, 'now make a 5 second video of a cat surfing' gets a generate plan for the cat and no 'needs Product photo' reply. '/lamp-turntable Halo floor lamp' plus a photo then gets a run_skill card again.

MEDIUM, retry heuristic orphan (confirmed). What is kept is now worked out from the last call backwards: a call is kept when it is the last of its kind, or when a later call that is kept used its output. This is a fixed point in one reverse pass, so A, B from A, A', B' from A' keeps A' and B'. The test runs the four generate calls through the real agent, each using the previous real output URL. It asserts the steps are exactly ['lamp second try', 'turn the second try'] with the chain kept, and the note says 2 earlier tries were left out.

LOW, type arrays in run_skill's schema: values and rows are now a string→string record. A number is coerced to its digits by z.preprocess, and the recipe's number inputs read digits as numbers, as a form does. Test: the run_skill api schema has no type array, values and rows items have additionalProperties {type:'string'}, and values.name = 42 validates and prices as '42 on a travertine plinth'.

LOW, dead attachment parsing: userWords now returns only the words, and the unused file list is gone. Attachments still become candidates when a kept call used them (W2's input candidates), as the tests assert.

LOW, the 'declined' match: lib/assist.ts exports DECLINED and REPLIED_INSTEAD, the agent's own decline results with the same text as before, plus declinedByUser(). draftFromThread counts only those as declined. Test: a generate error saying 'declined by the provider's safety system' is counted as 'didn't run', and the chat's own decline as 'you declined'.

fix.finalSummary: Skills W3 fix stage: both highs and both mediums are fixed, and all three lows are applied. Save as skill now matches each chat call to the generations it really made (the call's own generations items, now tagged with its tool_use id, or parsed from the real result shapes for older chats). So a Layers, Captions or Katana call that opened in its studio becomes one tool step with the exact input it ran with. A skill can never run a skill: the recipe schema refuses a run_skill step at save, file write and .zip import, and run_skill refuses to price, place or run from inside a skill's own work, so a price check can no longer recurse until it runs out of memory. The offline planner runs a recipe skill only when the message names it, so later requests in that chat are planned normally. Interleaved retries keep only the last tries. run_skill's values are plain text for every provider. Engines: everything was verified in demo mode on the mock provider. The studio tools ran on the open engine's routes with nothing connected (Layers, Captions and Katana demo jobs), and the generate and run_skill pipelines ran on cloud models in demo. Real runs need a fal or Replicate key (cloud) or a ComfyUI (open). Whether a live Claude, hosted or local model chooses run_skill is still unverified. Guests and accounts under public sign-up: unchanged by this stage. Assist, run_skill, Save as skill and its draft routes stay the owner's (assist-owner, OWNER_ALL for /api/mcp), and visitors see no new text.
left: Live-model use of run_skill (Claude, hosted, a local model) is still unverified, as in the implement stage.
A cross-call reference into or out of a studio step is still refused with the W7 message (by design for this package), so the 'dub then caption' story saves as two skills until W7.
The offline planner no longer auto-runs a project skill with a recipe unless the message names it (/name). Matching a recipe skill from free words ('do the dub thing') is left to the LLM agents.
Pre-existing and not from this package: 'Suggest names · Ollama' shows even when no local model answers (llmTextBackend). tsc needs a larger heap than the default on this tree.
